papers_read.title_as_printed: Deep Fusion of Brain Structure-Function in Mild Cognitive Impairment (Zhang L, Wang L, Gao J, Risacher SL, Yan J, Li G, Liu T, Zhu D; Medical Image Analysis 72 (2021) 102082)

Random walks on B distributed resting-state functional connectivity to identify Alzheimer’s disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment (Rahimiasl M, Moghadam Charkari N, Ghaderi F; Clinical Neurophysiology 132 (2021) 2540-2550)

what_each_reports.P-92: ADNI, 214 subjects (116 NC / 98 MCI) with T1, DTI and rs-fMRI; binary MCI vs NC. The model is a graph-based deep network (two-layer GCN) whose adjacency is initialised from the individual DTI structural connectome and updated with a learned rs-fMRI functional profile, with rs-fMRI Pearson correlations as node features (Destrieux, 148 regions). 5-fold cross-validation; dropout 0.6, batch normalisation, early stopping. Best setting (sigma 2.0, G(148,296)): accuracy Best 92.7%, Worst 83.3%, Ave 86.3%; precision 85.7, recall 80.6, specificity 89.9 (Table 4). A second ADNI subset from 28 other centres (124 subjects, 62 NC / 62 MCI) under the same 5-fold CV gives Best 94.1%, Ave 92.0% (Table 5). No AUC is reported anywhere, and the paper runs no concatenation baseline of its own; feature concatenation appears only as a prior-literature strategy in Related Work.
what_each_reports.P-97: ADNI, 125 subjects (36 HC / 30 EMCI / 33 LMCI / 26 AD; Table 2 prints AD = 25) with rs-fMRI; T1 is used only in preprocessing, and there is no DTI. Task: 4-class HC/EMCI/LMCI/AD. Method: HCP-MMP 360-region functional connectivity mapped with a B-distribution function, node2vec node embeddings (size 4) concatenated into one feature vector, then linear SVM and L2 logistic regression. Five-fold CV repeated 100 times. Accuracy 97.73% (SVM) / 97.32% (LR), quadratic weighted kappa 96.86% / 96.74%; without the mapping function, accuracy 87.2% / 86.96%. No AUC reported.

quantity_a: Classification accuracy for binary MCI vs NC from DTI + rs-fMRI connectome fusion, ADNI 214 subjects, 5-fold CV. The headline 92.7% is the Best column of the best setting; that setting's average is 86.3%.
quantity_b: Mean accuracy and quadratic weighted kappa over 100 repeats of 5-fold CV for 4-class HC/EMCI/LMCI/AD staging from rs-fMRI-only functional-connectivity embeddings, ADNI 125 subjects.
incompatible_if_same: No. Neither paper evaluates the other's method or claims an ordering the other refutes, and neither reports uncertainty for its headline. The record's own framing (91% vs 89%, 'marginal not fundamental difference') describes a small spread between two methods, which the adjudication reading lists as not incompatible. The figures the papers actually print (92.7% binary Best-column accuracy; 97.73% 4-class mean accuracy) are not estimates of one quantity.

gates.task: mismatch: P-92 is binary MCI vs NC (registry T1, MCI_vs_HC); P-97 is 4-class HC/EMCI/LMCI/AD (registry T3, multiclass_staging). The record's task_equivalence=true is wrong.
gates.dataset_family: match: both use ADNI (P-92: 214 subjects from 32 centres plus a 124-subject second set from 28 other centres; P-97: 125 subjects). Neither paper lets subject overlap be determined.
gates.validation_tier: match: both use internal cross-validation only (P-92 5-fold; P-97 5-fold repeated 100 times), i.e. V2. P-92's second ADNI set is a retrained replication, not external validation of a fixed model. The registry's Validation_Type 'not reported' for P-92 should be V2, and its Best_Metric 'not reported' should carry Acc 92.7. The record's 'same validation set' is false: the two samples and label sets differ.
gates.modality_family: mismatch: P-92 fuses diffusion MRI (DTI tractography connectome) with rs-fMRI; P-97 uses rs-fMRI only, with T1 in preprocessing. They share only the functional-MRI component. The registry's modality_subtype 'structural_MRI_only' for P-97 is wrong: its input is rs-fMRI connectivity.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: the endpoints differ (binary MCI vs NC against 4-class staging), and neither paper reports an AUC. P-92's headline accuracy is the Best column of its per-setting results (average 86.3%); P-97's is a mean over 100 repeats of 5-fold CV, accompanied by a quadratic kappa that P-92 does not compute.
performance_validity: The flag applies to P-97: 97.73% accuracy on internal cross-validation only, N = 125 split over four classes, no external cohort. Its results are therefore left out of cross-study performance comparisons, and a performance comparison resting on it cannot be genuine. The flag does not apply to P-92 (Best-column 92.7%, average 86.3%, below 0.97).
independence: Distinct author groups (UT Arlington, Indiana, UNC and Georgia vs Tarbiat Modares, Tehran). Both draw on ADNI, so the dataset family counts once, and participant overlap between P-92's 214/124-subject sets and P-97's 125 subjects is possible but cannot be determined from the papers.
grounds: Claim_a misreads P-92. P-92 reports accuracy, not AUC; its headline is 92.7% (the Best column for the best setting, average 86.3%) for binary MCI vs NC, and no 91% AUC appears. Only the dropout detail is correct (ratio 0.6).

Claim_b misreads P-97. P-97 uses rs-fMRI only (no DTI) and concatenates node2vec node embeddings from a single functional graph rather than DTI and fMRI features. It reports accuracy and quadratic kappa, not AUC (97.73% for a 4-class task), on its own 125-subject sample, not 'the same validation set' as P-92.
The record itself describes no disagreement: its resolution note calls the gap expected and 'marginal not fundamental', which is a spread between two methods rather than a contradiction.

Read against the documents, the pair holds no incompatible claim either: the tasks differ (binary vs 4-class), as do the modality sets (DTI + fMRI vs fMRI) and the accuracy summaries (Best column vs repeated-CV mean). P-97 also meets the performance-validity exclusion, so the pair could not be genuine even if re-drafted.

record_defects: claim_a '91% AUC': P-92 reports no AUC in its text, tables or figure captions. Its headline is accuracy, 92.7% (Best column of the best setting; average 86.3%), and on the second ADNI subset 94.1% (average 92.0%). The dropout detail is correct (ratio 0.6).

claim_b 'DTI + rs-fMRI simple concatenation': P-97 uses no DTI (rs-fMRI only, with T1 in preprocessing). Its concatenation is of node2vec node embeddings from one functional graph, not multimodal feature concatenation.
claim_b '89% AUC': P-97 reports no AUC. It gives accuracy 97.73% (SVM) / 97.32% (LR) with its mapping function and 87.2% / 86.96% without, and quadratic kappa 96.86% / 96.74%.
claim_b 'on same validation set' is false: P-97 used its own 125-subject ADNI sample with four classes; P-92 used 214 (and 124) subjects with two classes.
task_equivalence=true is false: binary MCI vs NC against 4-class HC/EMCI/LMCI/AD.
modality_family 'functional_mri' with modality_family_equal 'Yes' overstates the match: P-92 is a DTI + rs-fMRI fusion, P-97 is rs-fMRI only.
apparent_performance_gap '2 percentage points (91% vs 89%)': neither figure is in either paper, and the headline accuracies the papers do print (92.7% binary; 97.73% 4-class) are not comparable.

resolution_note 'both approaches are variants of DTI+fMRI fusion' and 'Graph representation > concatenation' are false: P-97 is not a fusion method, and it is itself a graph-embedding method (node2vec random walks on a functional connectivity graph).

Provenance: the record's claims and note are unchanged since its first commit (087db63, 2026-03-28). At that commit the summary blocks already gave P-92 as 92.7% accuracy for MCI vs NC and P-97 as 97.73% accuracy / 96.86% kappa for 4-class staging, so the 91%/89% AUC figures were not taken from the blocks.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in these two papers. Neither reports an AUC or a DTI + rs-fMRI concatenation result, and neither makes a claim the other contradicts. A re-drafted record using the papers' real figures would be documented incommensurability (task, modality set and accuracy summary all differ) and would in any case rest on P-97, which meets the performance-validity exclusion. Only a different paper pairing, not a re-reading of these two, could produce a genuine candidate.
